note: Sources assessed and declined, with what was found. Declining after looking is a result; declining without looking is a gap.

declined.source: Antenati — the nine sitemaps other than ant_archivio
looked: story_location-sitemap.xml — 59 urls, story TAGS (Alfenas, Americana, Bari) marking where a family story is set
ant_storia-sitemap.xml + 2 — 140 family stories and blog posts
post-sitemap, dmc_users_nationality, story_author, story_nationality — editorial taxonomy
declined.why: Antenati's remaining sitemaps carry the portal's magazine — family stories, author pages, the nationality tags on them. Charming, and not a statement about where any record is held. The one sitemap that was archival, ant_archivio, gave all 119 state archives and has been harvested. There is no second file here.

declined.name: IrishGenealogy.ie — bulk harvest of its record locations
declined.verdict: declined by this project, not by the site
declined.why: Behind a Cloudflare MANAGED CHALLENGE. It loads perfectly in a human's browser and answers 403 to everything else, and its own challenge page carries «noindex, nofollow» — that is a site saying plainly that it does not want to be read by a script. Working around a bot gate is not something this project will do, whatever the data is worth. IrishGenealogy stays what it already is here: a provider row with a link a human clicks, and it is the best free national source in these islands. The record-location question it was asked to answer is answered instead by Townlands.ie, which publishes the whole county–barony–civil parish–townland hierarchy as an open download. See scripts/harvest-ireland.py.
